label: the overflow guard is raised past the point the integrand itself overflows
equivalent: exp(s^2) overflows f64 at s^2 = 709.78, that is s = 26.641, which is BELOW the 26.7 the guard uses. For any hi in (26.7, 100] the substituted branch is always entered (split is at most max(1, lo) < hi) and its last panel evaluates g at x close to hi^2 >= 712 > 709.78, so `x.exp()` is already +inf, `total` becomes +inf by addition, and the function returns Some(f64::INFINITY) — the same value the guard returns. Below 26.641 neither form fires. The only observable difference is how many panels the loop walks, which no test measures.

label: the noise half's substitution begins at the wrong lower limit when the reset is also far below the mean
the substituted integrand drops the Jacobian of s = sqrt(x)
the panels on the substituted axis are twenty-five times too wide
equivalent: The width of 2 carries about fifteen decades of margin, and 50 is still inside it. For `exp` on a panel of width h, 24-point Gauss-Legendre has relative error bounded by exp((h/4)(rho + 1/rho) - 48 ln rho - h/2) over Bernstein ellipses rho, minimised at rho = 8n/h; at h = 50 that is rho = 3.84 and exp(-38.4) = 2e-17, below f64 epsilon, and the rule only starts to lose digits near h = 100 (1.5e-9). The only non-entire factor is 1/(2 sqrt(x)), whose branch point at x = 0 sits at rho >= 1.33 for the widest panel the substitution can produce, contributing rho^-48 = 1.3e-6 of a term of size O(1) against a panel integral of at least e^51 - i.e. 1e-27 relative. Measured as well as bounded: over a 500-point grid of (p, q) covering the whole sub-threshold half (hi from 1.2 to 26.5, lo from 0 to hi) the largest relative difference between the two widths is 1.5e-13, and it occurs where the integral is of order 1e280 and the implementation's OWN disagreement with an independent 600-panel uniform rule on the unsubstituted w axis is 1.4e-13, with that reference's own 300-to-600-panel convergence 2e-13 - the difference is the rounding of the panel sum, not quadrature error. Over the 713 grid points the worst disagreement with that reference is 1.88e-13 for the mutant and 1.4e-13 for the implementation, and where the integral is below 1e100 they are 3.1e-14 and 4.5e-15 - the same order, and both under the reference's own convergence. One shape of test could still see it: at some points, (p, q) = (-6.69, -4.15) among them, the implementation happens to agree with the 600-panel reference to the last bit and the mutant does not, so an assertion of BIT equality against one particular reference would separate them. That is a coincidence of rounding rather than a property - it depends on the panel count the reference is given and on the last-place rounding of exp, sqrt and erfcx on one target, and this crate is built for several - so this is recorded as equivalent for every test that compares values with a tolerance, which is every test a portable crate can carry. What the mutation does leave behind is the margin: the width of 2 is about fifteen decades tighter than this integrand needs.
